sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: DeepSeek Harness (dsh) is an open-source agent harness from DeepSeek AI. It runs an AI agent you control through a local web interface, and almost everything in it is a plugin.
sixtySeconds.problem: Agent tools often bundle fixed features that are hard to change. DeepSeek Harness is built on an everything-is-a-plugin design using the Cordis framework, so parts can be added or swapped.
whoFor: Developers experimenting with AI agent harnesses
People who want to run DeepSeek's agent locally in a browser UI
Plugin authors building on an extensible agent
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if you want to try DeepSeek's own agent harness and are comfortable with a developer preview that will change. For a stable daily tool, a mature harness is safer for now.
requirements: pnpm and Git if running from source

overview: DeepSeek Harness is an agent harness developed by DeepSeek AI. It uses Cordis, a plugin framework, so features are plugins that can be composed. Community plugins can be tagged with the dsh-plugin GitHub topic.
It runs a Web UI on your machine, by default at http://127.0.0.1:3080, and opens it in your browser on a local launch. Over SSH it only prints the URL.
The project is in developer preview and the README warns that there will be compatibility-breaking changes. It also asks you to read its safety notice before running it.

steps.title: Start the Web UI
steps.body: Opens http://127.0.0.1:3080 in your browser. Add --no-open to only start the server.

steps.title: Clone and build
steps.code:
git clone https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness.git
cd deepseek-harness
pnpm install
pnpm run build
